title: A chart power clears the conormal transition coefficients
statement: Let $R$ and $\bar C$ be commutative rings, let $\pi\in R$, and give $\bar C$ both an $R$-algebra structure and an $R/(\pi^2)$-algebra structure. Let $d$ be finite polynomial data with $n,m,r\in\mathbb N$, $f_i,a_s,h_{sit},g_{si}\in R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, finite subsets $E_s\subseteq\operatorname{Fin}(m)$, and presentation map as in [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-lift-preparation], and assume the structure $d.\mathrm{Prepared}$ of that node (in particular its cleared polynomial relations and specified localized conormal bases). No Noetherian hypothesis on $R$ or compatible scalar-tower hypothesis is needed for this assertion. For $k,k^{\prime}\in\operatorname{Fin}(r)$, $l,j\in\operatorname{Fin}(m)$ with $j\in E_k$, set $b_j=a_{k^{\prime}}h_{klj}-\sum_{t\in E_{k^{\prime}}}h_{k^{\prime}lt}h_{ktj}$. Then there exists $N\in\mathbb N$ such that $a_k^N b_j\in(f_i\mid i\in\operatorname{Fin}(m))+(\pi^2)$ in $R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, where $(\pi^2)$ is generated by the constant polynomial. Localization and its canonical map have the meanings of [def-weil-ring-localization-away] and [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away].

proof.text: Let P=(R/(pi^2))[x], I=(reduced(f_i)), A=P/I, L=A[1/ak], M=(I/I^2)[1/ak], and sigma:R[x] to L the composite reduction, quotient and localization map. Reducing hd.relation kills the pi^2 term. Regard the resulting identity as an equality in the ideal I, apply toCotangent and the localized-module map, and use scalar towers. Thus sigma(a_s) w_i=sum_{t in E_s} sigma(h_sit) w_t for every s,i, where w_i is the localized conormal class of f_i.

proof.text: Fix j in E_k and apply the j-th coordinate of the specified conormal basis. Since the coordinate of w_t for t in E_k is delta_tj, the k-th relation gives sigma(a_k) c(w_i)=sigma(h_kij). The k-prime relation gives sigma(a_kprime)c(w_l)=sum_t sigma(h_kprime,lt)c(w_t). Multiply this last equality by sigma(a_k), substitute the preceding identity for i=l and for each t, and commute the factors. The result is sigma(b_j)=0 for b_j=a_kprime*h_klj-sum_t h_kprime,lt*h_ktj.

proof.text: Apply the localization equality criterion to the zero image of the class of reduced(b_j) in L. It supplies N with ak^N times that class zero in A. The quotient zero criterion therefore puts reduced(a_k^N*b_j) in I.

proof.text: Let F=(f_i) in R[x]. Coefficient reduction red is surjective by MvPolynomial.map_surjective and has red(F)=I by Ideal.map_span. Mathlib Ideal.comap_map_of_surjective gives red inverse image of I equal to F plus ker(red). MvPolynomial.ker_map, Ideal.mk_ker and Ideal.map_span identify ker(red) with (C(pi^2)). Hence a_k^N*b_j belongs to the asserted ideal sum.

theorem conormal_transition_coefficients
    {R : Type a} {Cbar : Type c} [CommRing R] [CommRing Cbar] [Algebra R Cbar] {π : R}
    [Algebra (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({π ^ 2} : Set R)) Cbar]
    (d : PopescuLiftPresentation R Cbar π) (hd : d.Prepared)
    (k k' : Fin d.r) (l j : Fin d.m) (hj : j ∈ d.E k) :
    ∃ N : ℕ, d.a k ^ N *
        (d.a k' * d.h k l j - ∑ j' ∈ d.E k', d.h k' l j' * d.h k j' j) ∈
      Ideal.span (Set.range d.f) ⊔
        Ideal.span ({MvPolynomial.C (π ^ 2)} : Set (MvPolynomial (Fin d.n) R))
